articles.summary: The timber-framed structure designed by Marlon Blackwell Architects for the U.S. Pavilion at the 2025 Venice Architecture Biennale will be reconstructed at Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art in Bentonville , Arkansas, in late 2027. articles.title: Dual-Family House / Khuon Studio
articles.summary: This unique project came to Khuôn Studio through an inspiring brief from a very distinctive client. The homeowner envisioned a house where two families could live together while maintaining their own independence and privacy. His desire was to create a home entirely covered in a grey cementitious finish, complemented by the lush greenery of tropical plants that he had carefully collected over time. The remaining spirit of the tropical house was entrusted to the creativity and architectural interpretation of Khuôn Studio.

articles.title: Skin of Skin House / CANs architecture studio
articles.summary: Set in Yunlin, Taiwan, the project sits on the peri-urban edge of the region's plains—an in-between landscape where farming fields and small-town infrastructure overlap. In a subtropical climate of heat, humidity, and strong solar exposure, corrugated metal sheets and light-gauge steel frames have long been common in everyday buildings and agricultural structures for simple reasons: they are affordable, quick to assemble, and resilient in extreme weather.

articles.title: When Acoustic Control Needs to Move
articles.summary: Acoustic design is often associated with permanent building elements, such as walls, roofs, ceilings, and insulation systems, which help control how sound travels through a space. However, not all noise sources or environments are permanent. A construction site changes as work progresses; machinery is replaced or relocated from one area to another; an industrial space may incorporate new equipment; and a temporary work area may emerge in a space that was never designed to accommodate it. For this latter situation, Japanese stationery company Kokuyo detected a problem. In 2022, the company sought feedback from junior high and high school students on what their study-time paint points were. articles.title: A Bauhausian Take on the Coat Rack
articles.summary: This wonderful, Bauhausian Bazar coat rack is by German industrial designer Steffen Kehrle. By transforming the tree into a wire cylinder, Kehrle provides hanging space on the outside, while the interior becomes usable storage space thanks to circular shelves. The shelves can be placed wherever there's a hoop; it's up to the user. My only gripe is that I wish it came with more hooks that the user could place. If I owned one of these, I'd probably DIY some up. Made of powder-coated steel wire, the Bazar is in production by German furniture brand Richard Lampert.

articles.title: A Simple, Versatile, "Handy" Mobile Furniture Piece
articles.summary: This Handy furniture piece is by Taiwanese industrial designer Hsinhung Chou . It's such a simple and useful form factor that I'm surprised I haven't seen it before; I think it'd be useful for everything from gardening to picknicking to household chores and handyman jobs. When I'm outdoors on my property, for instance, I often wish I had a way to carry tools that also offered a table-height surface to work on whatever component I'm repairing.
